free_tier.stated: No storage quota. Per-file ceiling is a single setting: 'Maximum File Upload Size (in bytes) ... Use -1 to remove the limit.'
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: extraction found no retention clause; the seed's limits text may still state one, see extras.limits_verbatim

egress.terms: Your own infrastructure. Cloud-hosted workspaces have a storage limit visible in the admin panel, but self-managed does not.

tooling: Rocket.Chat REST API `POST /api/v1/rooms.media/{rid}` + `rooms.mediaConfirm`. Storage backends: GridFS (MongoDB, default), AmazonS3/MinIO, Google Cloud Storage, WebDAV, FileSystem. The WebDAV and S3 backends make it pluggable into anything.
chaining: N workspaces x unlimited rooms. The WebDAV backend is the interesting bit: it turns Rocket.Chat into a front-end over any WebDAV store, so it chains rather than multiplies.
limits_note: Starter: up to 50 users, self-managed. Community: up to 100 concurrent users, self-hosted only, 10,000 push notifications/month. Per-file limit unlimited if set to -1.

identity_cost.detail: no identity_cost field and no identity statement in the source record; defaulted to email and flagged, not evidence

reliability_note: Solid; the default GridFS backend stores blobs inside MongoDB, which is a poor choice at TB scale (the docs themselves recommend S3/MinIO). Files can be JWT-protected or public per workspace setting.
